1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Practice S-T-O-P (Sit, Think, Observe, Plan) immediately when lost, prioritizing shelter and warmth first because hypothermia strikes within three hours.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. S - SIT Down Immediately & Breathe: Panic is the #1 wilderness killer; sit down for 5 full minutes, drink water, eat a snack, and calm your heart rate.
2. T - THINK Through Timeline & Assets: Inventory your Ten Essentials, daylight hours remaining before sunset, weather trend, and the trip plan left at home.
3. O - OBSERVE Terrain & Natural Shelter: Scan for wind-protected high dry ground away from widowmaker dead limbs, dry flash-flood washes, and avalanche chutes.
4. P - PLAN Before Dark (Rule of 3s): Prioritize (1) First Aid, (2) Insulated Shelter before dark (3 hr rule), (3) Fire & Water (3 day rule), (4) Distress Signals.
1.worked_field_example: In 40 F wind and rain, building a dry insulated shelter and putting on a rain shell takes priority over rationing food or hiking blindly.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: Inspect the Ten Essentials survival kit flat-lay and rank the top three items needed during the first 30 minutes of an unexpected night out.
1.real_world_connection_box: U.S. Forest Service & NOLS Survival Standard: Practice S-T-O-P (Sit, Think, Observe, Plan) immediately when lost, prioritizing shelter and warmth first because hypothermia strikes within three hours.

primary_source_citation.title: U.S. Search & Rescue Task Force & NOLS Technical Reference: Stopping All Four Body Heat-Loss Mechanisms in an Emergency Shelter

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Cold damp ground steals body heat 25 times faster than still air by conduction, making a 6-inch compressed dry leaf bed essential.
core_mechanism_bullets: Conduction (Direct Ground Contact): Insulate underneath first with 6 to 8 inches of compressed pine boughs, dry leaves, or a closed-cell foam pad.
Convection (Wind Stripping Warm Air): Pitch low A-frame debris hut perpendicular to wind with 3-foot leaf walls and zero unnecessary dead air volume.
Radiation (Infrared Loss from Head/Neck): An uncovered head and neck radiate up to 30 to 40 percent of resting body heat in freezing air; put on an insulated beanie.
Evaporation (Sweat & Wet Cotton): Cotton loses 90 percent of insulation when wet ('Cotton Kills'); ventilate layers while building shelter so you never soak base layers.
2.worked_field_example: An A-frame debris hut sized just larger than your shoulders with 6 inches of dry ground duff retains core heat without a campfire.
2.counselor_tabletop_demo: Compare hand warmth on bare cold stone versus a 4-inch pad of compressed dry leaves and pine needles after 60 seconds.
2.real_world_connection_box: U.S. Search & Rescue & NOLS Shelter Standard: Cold damp ground steals body heat 25 times faster than still air by conduction, making a 6-inch compressed dry leaf bed essential.
2.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + U.S. Search & Rescue Task Force & NOLS

primary_source_citation.title: U.S. Coast Guard & ICAO Search and Rescue Manual Technical Reference: Day & Night Distress Signals: Mirror Aiming & Ground Symbols

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Three blasts on a pealess rescue whistle or three smoky fires in a triangle form the universal international distress signal.
core_mechanism_bullets: Signal Mirror Finger-V Sight (10+ Miles): Hold mirror near chin, bounce sunlight onto outstretched V-fingers framing the distant aircraft, and wiggle flash across cockpit.
Universal 3-Blast Whistle Signal: A pealess 115 dB plastic whistle carries 1 to 2 miles with minimal energy long after shouting destroys your voice.
Three Signal Fires in a Triangle: Daytime: heap green pine boughs on hot flames for thick white smoke; Nighttime: burn dry crisp wood on an open ridge.
High-Contrast Ground Symbols (30+ Ft): Trample or lay 30-foot-tall letters (minimum 6:1 length-to-width ratio): V = Require Assistance, X = Require Medical Help.
3.worked_field_example: A 100-decibel pealess whistle carries over 1 mile through dense timber without exhausting your voice, while a 15-foot ground X alerts aircraft.
3.counselor_tabletop_demo: Sight a distant target through the center star hole of a signal mirror and align the reflected light dot onto two outstretched fingers.
3.real_world_connection_box: U.S. Coast Guard & ICAO Distress Signal Standard: Three blasts on a pealess rescue whistle or three smoky fires in a triangle form the universal international distress signal. An aimed star-hole signal mirror reflects a focused sunbeam visible to search aircraft more than 10 miles away.

primary_source_citation.source_agency: CDC Backcountry Water Treatment Guide & EPA
primary_source_citation.title: CDC Backcountry Water Treatment Guide & EPA Technical Reference: Backcountry Water Disinfection Methods & Pathogen Protection

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: A rolling boil for 1 full minute (or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet elevation) inactivates 100 percent of waterborne pathogens.
core_mechanism_bullets: Method 1: Rolling Boil (Gold Standard): 1 full minute at sea level (3 minutes above 6,500 ft) neutralizes all viruses, bacteria, Giardia, and Cryptosporidium oocysts.
Method 2: 0.1-Micron Hollow-Fiber Filter: Physically strains out bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella) and protozoa (Giardia, Crypto) immediately; pair with drops if viruses suspected.
Method 3: Chlorine Dioxide Tablets: Effective against viruses, bacteria, and Giardia in 30 minutes (wait 4 hours in cold turbid water for Cryptosporidium).
Pre-Filter Turbid Water Through Bandana: Always pour cloudy creek water through a clean cloth first so sediment does not clog filter pores or shield microbes.
4.worked_field_example: When treating glacial meltwater at 8,000 feet, strain sediment through a bandana first and maintain a rolling boil for 3 full minutes.
4.counselor_tabletop_demo: Trace the three-stage treatment sequence from cloth pre-filtration through a 0.1-micron hollow-fiber filter to a rolling camp boil.
4.real_world_connection_box: CDC & U.S. EPA Backcountry Water Treatment Standard: A rolling boil for 1 full minute (or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet elevation) inactivates 100 percent of waterborne pathogens. Pre-filtering turbid stream water through cloth prevents silt from clogging a 0.1-micron hollow-fiber microfilter.
4.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + CDC Backcountry Water Guide & U.S. EPA
4.bespoke_visual_caption: Three-stage water purification cutaway showing cloth pre-filtration, a 0.1-micron hollow-fiber filter cartridge, and a rolling camp boil.
4.v47_slide_title: CDC & U.S. EPA Backcountry Water Treatment Standard
